nodes.label: desktop memory - the v2 chunking and structure model

Frozen copy taken 2026-08-03 of the desktop machine's memory file - the live directory sits on the other machine and is not reachable from here, so this copy is what there is to review. Listed unreviewed in REVIEW_REGISTER.md section 6. The v2 chunking and structure model, converged with the user 2026-06-01, replacing v1's chunker. The decisions: a chunk is a coherent episode, NOT a fixed-size window, killing v1's fill-to-budget batching because it smears facets that only mean something on a coherent unit; build chunks by descending the source's own structure, then group leaf-level conversation and prose by coherence; the token budget is a guardrail and ceiling only, never the grouping rule, and the number is trivial, picked later; an over-budget episode splits into subchunks that ARE just chunks, 1 becoming 1.1, 1.2, 1.3, with NO parent node and no episode node, the episode existing only as the chunks sharing a path prefix, reconstructed on demand - the user killed the parent explicitly; split priority is the finest coherence seam first, with a blunt size cut only at the floor; the index is a materialized path stored as integer components, [1,2,3] rather than the string '1.2.3' so 1.10 does not missort and prefix-match stays clean, replacing the flat ordinal and NEXT that v1 chunks have; the path carries POSITION only, with the meaning or type of each level living in the probe's recovered shape schema - path says where, schema says what; the path does triple duty as structural ancestry, context expansion by prefix, and duplicate-collapse and diversity by prefix; 'records versus prose' is per-POSITION in the tree rather than a per-file classification; and context comes from the graph around the chunk rather than from fat chunks or overlap, with NO overlap because it fights references-not-copies.
